chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Abu Ayyub, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever says
a hundred times, his deed is the best of the people's deeds that day, except for one who recites it more.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: The declaration of monotheism (There is no god but God)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting La ilaha illallah one hundred times?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the immense spiritual weight of *Tasbih* (glorification) in Shia devotional practice, emphasizing that consistency in this simple act yields superior reward. The comparative nature of the phrase 'unless someone else recites it more' underscores the dynamic meritocracy of worship, where greater devotion yields greater status. This narration serves as a foundational text for the daily recitation of *La ilaha illallah* as a means of purifying the soul and securing divine favor.
